headline: High: xonsh can write and egress broadly while the zoomcamp profile is a non-runnable course artifact, so pairwise risks center on xonsh-driven leakage and workflow conflicts rather than direct bidirectional agent interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented: agent_a is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while agent_b uses stdin/stdout and filesystem but no clipboard or MCP. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or files created by xonsh and later read by the course materials, which is an unusual configuration with limited blast radius.
conditions: IF operator manually copies xonsh output into course prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem is introduced between the two, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the course repo and shell session separate.
Avoid copy-pasting untrusted shell output into prompts.
Use read-only mounts for course materials.
Add a manual review step before reusing generated text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b can read and write the filesystem and egress broadly, so any sensitive files in its workspace can leave the environment. agent_a touches no data classes and has no egress, so it is not the leakage source; the pair risk comes from xonsh handling local files while the course artifact offers no protective boundary.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the xonsh workspace, they can be read and exfiltrated.
IF the course materials are placed in the same writable directory, they may be copied or uploaded by xonsh.
mitigations: Store secrets outside the xonsh workspace.
Use a dedicated non-sensitive working directory.
Disable network access at the container or host level for the session.
Mount course files read-only.
Review shell history before sharing logs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b has write_filesystem and execute_shell, but agent_a is a non-runnable course profile with no write or concurrency surface, so there is no documented write-write conflict between the pair. The only overlap is conceptual data-engineering content, not mutable shared resources.
conditions: IF both are placed on the same writable directory, xonsh can overwrite course artifacts.
IF an external orchestrator gives agent_a write access not shown in the profile, conflict risk would rise.
mitigations: Use separate directories for course content and shell work.
Make the course repo read-only.
Avoid concurrent edits from multiple sessions.
Snapshot files before running shell workflows.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a course repository, not an acting agent, so it cannot authoritatively feed decisions into agent_b by default. agent_b can execute shell commands, but there is no documented pipeline where it consumes agent_a outputs automatically; the cascade is therefore limited to manual reuse of course text or examples.
conditions: IF operator treats course examples as authoritative operational instructions, xonsh may execute them incorrectly.
IF generated shell output is copied into downstream automation, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Verify commands before execution.
Treat course examples as illustrative, not authoritative.
Run commands in a disposable shell session.
Require human review before automation.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is documented: agent_a touches no regulated data classes and agent_b lists general development data classes only. Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, and there is no evidence of PHI, EU PII, residency, or retention conflicts in the pair.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into the workspace, compliance review is needed.
IF deployment policies require specific residency or retention controls, those must be checked separately.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention settings for any logs.
Review deployment residency requirements.
Use separate environments for sensitive workloads.
